author: Ren
endorsement: Not Fernando's opinion. Claims and dispositions require his review before becoming his substance.

disposition_definitions.stop_line: Do not repeat publicly until corrected or validated.
disposition_definitions.reconstruct: The question is useful but the current measure is not valid for it.
disposition_definitions.test: Keep explicitly as a hypothesis with a registered validation path.
disposition_definitions.retain_scoped: Retain only with the scope and caveats in this ledger.
disposition_definitions.missing: Required for the project goal but absent from the current instrument.

evidence_grades.A: Direct primary data or a validated official measure appropriate to the claim.
evidence_grades.B: Strong primary research or official modelling with material limitations.
evidence_grades.C: Indirect evidence, analogy, partial construct validity or unvalidated extrapolation.
evidence_grades.D: Unsupported, invalidly measured or contradicted by the method used.

claims.title: Capability promises contain conditions
claims.claim: Every meaningful promise of capability or agency is conditional on one or more technical, economic, institutional, operational, human, ecological or geopolitical factors.
claims.rationale: This is a strong organising grammar, not yet an established universal empirical law.
counter_hypotheses: Some capabilities are sufficiently unconditional that the added IFs do not change meaningful access.
The useful unit is an outcome-production system rather than a capability promise.
falsifiers: Repeated service studies find that the proposed condition taxonomy does not explain observed access failures.
Independent reviewers cannot classify real access paths consistently using the IF grammar.
claims.next_test: Encode ten services with independent reviewers and measure agreement, omitted conditions and decision usefulness.

claims.title: Money is the biggest IF
claims.claim: Affordability is currently the dominant constraint on broad human access.
claims.rationale: Poverty and financial-hardship evidence supports importance, but dominance varies by service, cohort and jurisdiction.
counter_hypotheses: Capacity, eligibility, information, distance, quality or trust dominates for important services.
A condition called affordability is partly a symptom of unequal income, ownership and public provision.
falsifiers: Removing consumer financial burden leaves effective use and outcomes mostly unchanged.
Service funnels repeatedly identify a non-financial stage as the largest loss.
claims.next_test: Estimate service-level access funnels for the pilot cohort and compare losses by condition.

claims.title: $30 a day is a developed-world floor
claims.claim: $30 per day in 2021 PPP is a defensible developed-world floor and 80% below it are on the wrong side of the money condition.
claims.rationale: PIP can estimate the headcount at a chosen line, but $30 is not an official developed-world floor and survey welfare can be income or consumption. A headcount does not establish effective access.
counter_hypotheses: Local reference budgets and observed deprivation classify adequate living standards differently.
Public and household production permits effective access below the selected monetary line.
falsifiers: The $30 classification has weak agreement with material deprivation and service-access outcomes.
Sensitivity to PPP vintage, welfare concept or threshold reverses the public conclusion.
claims.next_test: Compare $30 headcounts with local reference-budget shortfalls and deprivation outcomes across representative countries.

claims.title: Global uplift costs 62% of GDP
claims.claim: Lifting 6.64 billion people below $30 per day to that level costs $72.7 trillion per year, about 62% of global GDP.
claims.rationale: The calculation applies the full threshold to every person below it, equivalent to assuming zero resources for all. It must sum shortfalls from the line.
counter_hypotheses: The aggregate poverty gap is materially smaller than the full-line-times-headcount estimate.
Income, consumption, in-kind provision and behavioural responses make a static transfer calculation incomplete.
falsifiers: A reproducible PIP distribution calculation using the correct poverty-gap definition produces the same estimate within a predeclared tolerance.
claims.next_test: Compute the aggregate shortfall from PIP version 20260324_2021 and publish code, welfare concepts, coverage and uncertainty.

claims.title: Only cost collapse closes the gap
claims.claim: The only arithmetic capable of closing the global access gap is the cost of a decent life falling.
claims.rationale: The conclusion relies partly on MF-C004 and excludes mixed mechanisms without comparison.
counter_hypotheses: A portfolio of earnings, transfers, public provision, ownership reform, productivity and lower costs closes the gap.
For capacity-constrained services, more funding and supply matter more than marginal cost collapse.
falsifiers: Cross-country or microsimulation evidence shows feasible mixed mechanisms reaching the selected access floor without broad cost collapse.
claims.next_test: Compare policy and production portfolios using distributional microsimulation and service-capacity constraints.

claims.title: Wages and prices are the transmission channels
claims.claim: Productivity gains reach households through wages or prices.
claims.origin: Fernando-endorsed framing, later expanded in the commissioned proposal
claims.rationale: Transfers, taxes, self-employment, capital income, debt, wealth, public provision, household production and time costs also transmit or block gains.
counter_hypotheses: Public provision is the dominant transmission channel for some essential services.
Ownership and capital income dominate gains for some households while liabilities absorb gains for others.
falsifiers: A complete household accounting decomposition shows omitted channels are quantitatively negligible across relevant cohorts.
claims.next_test: Build a full household resource and service-provision identity before choosing headline channels.

claims.title: The world is not in an Engels' Pause
claims.claim: World real GDP per capita and derived real labour income per capita differed by 3.5 index points from 2004 to 2025, so the world is not in an Engels' Pause.
claims.rationale: The two lines are dimensionally consistent with each other, but not like-for-like with output per worker and real wages in Allen. GDP deflation, composition, modelling and cohort aggregation limit the inference.
counter_hypotheses: Specific occupations, regions or income groups are already experiencing pause-like divergence hidden by the world average.
Household purchasing-power income diverges more than GDP-deflated aggregate labour income.
falsifiers: Like-for-like cohort measures with household deflation and uncertainty confirm broad tracking across exposed groups.
Alternative aggregation and vintage choices leave the conclusion unchanged.
claims.next_test: Decompose by employment, hours, real hourly compensation, population and cohort, then compare with a reconstructed historical benchmark.

claims.title: Access is the product of five factors
claims.claim: Access equals availability multiplied by affordability, eligibility, quality and delivery, and becomes zero if any factor is zero.
claims.rationale: The dimensions are useful, but multiplying unlike scores without a common conditional-probability interpretation creates fake precision and hidden weighting.
counter_hypotheses: A sequential service funnel identifies access losses more faithfully.
Different dimensions are partly substitutable or jointly determined rather than independent.
falsifiers: Each term is estimated as a conditional probability for the same need, cohort, service and period, and the product validates against realised effective access.
claims.next_test: Construct one service funnel and validate predicted access against observed use and outcome.

claims.title: Zero-cost count measures abundance
claims.claim: The number of products and services at near-zero consumer or delivery cost is an appropriate target for abundance.
claims.rationale: A count ignores relevance, reach, outcome and costs shifted to taxpayers, advertisers, data, attention, time, unpaid labour or nature.
counter_hypotheses: Effective-access coverage by important outcome better reflects abundance.
Required labour hours or total social cost is more decision-useful than a binary zero threshold.
falsifiers: The count predicts independently measured access, agency and well-being after controlling for service mix and population reach.
claims.next_test: Compare count, cost-to-outcome, coverage and consumer-time measures across a pilot basket.

claims.title: The binding IF migrates to permission
claims.claim: As technical cost falls, legality, identity, jurisdiction and certification become the primary access constraints for many services.
claims.rationale: Plausible for regulated services, but service-specific and confounded with capacity, trust, quality and infrastructure.
counter_hypotheses: Physical capacity, complements and quality remain binding after digital costs fall.
Regulation harmonises as capability diffuses, so permission gaps narrow.
falsifiers: Across low-cost services, non-permission constraints consistently explain more unmet need.
Cross-jurisdiction eligibility variance falls after cost decline.
claims.next_test: Track a single regulated service across jurisdictions and estimate condition-specific losses over time.

claims.title: ADKAR phases describe civilisation-scale transition
claims.claim: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability and Reinforcement provide the right sequence for a multi-decade social transition.
claims.rationale: ADKAR is an individual and organisational change tool. Cohort desynchronisation is useful; macro phase prediction is not validated.
counter_hypotheses: Technology diffusion, institutional capacity or political conflict predicts transition better.
Cohorts move non-sequentially and regress in ways the phase model obscures.
falsifiers: Observed cohorts do not pass through the stages in the proposed order.
Alternative models produce better out-of-sample transition forecasts.
claims.next_test: Use ADKAR only as a communication diagnostic and compare it with diffusion and institutional-readiness models.

claims.title: Five crisis crossings forecast social response
claims.claim: Credibility, local displacement, legitimacy, essential work and permission-border breaks are the principal foreseeable transition crises.
claims.rationale: These are coherent scenarios, not validated forecasts. Ecological, fiscal, security, model-failure, misinformation and democratic-governance paths may be missing.
counter_hypotheses: Different crises dominate or the five categories are consequences rather than forecastable events.
The proposed leading signals fire too late or too often to support action.
falsifiers: Historical backtests show poor lead time, low discrimination or unacceptable false-alarm costs.
Prospective observations are better explained by omitted crisis pathways.
claims.next_test: Backtest each pathway against automation, industrial closure, pandemic and cost-of-living episodes before setting thresholds.

claims.title: Pre-committed triggers improve transition outcomes
claims.claim: Public thresholds with pre-agreed owners, actions and finance will reduce harm from transition shocks.
claims.rationale: Adaptive social protection supports the mechanism for recurrent shocks, but transferability to AI labour shocks and false-alarm costs are unknown.
counter_hypotheses: Rigid triggers are gamed, activate too late or crowd out better discretionary judgement.
Political and delivery capacity, rather than trigger design, determines outcomes.
falsifiers: Backtests and rehearsals show more delay, exclusion or net harm than a transparent discretionary baseline.
claims.next_test: Compare candidate rules through historical backtests and a tabletop with delivery operators and affected workers.

claims.title: Positive agency is a required outcome
claims.claim: The Observatory must measure gained choice and capability, not only avoided crisis and material consumption.
claims.rationale: The current instrument is hazard-heavy and can report safety while autonomy, time, voice, connection or environmental sustainability deteriorates.
counter_hypotheses: Material access alone is a sufficient operational proxy for agency.
Subjective choice measures are too unstable for decision use.
falsifiers: Agency measures add no predictive or explanatory value for well-being, consent or resilience beyond material access.
claims.next_test: Add desired versus actual time use, perceived control, civic voice, learning access and service choice to the pilot validation set.

claims.title: Headline CPI must become negative
claims.claim: Abundance requires consumer price inflation to become negative for real household baskets.
claims.rationale: Target outcomes can become cheaper in quality-adjusted or labour-time terms while aggregate CPI remains positive.
counter_hypotheses: Broad access improves through income and quality gains with stable positive aggregate inflation.
Demonetised digital services are poorly represented in expenditure-weighted CPI.
falsifiers: Across countries and periods, broad effective-access gains occur only alongside negative household-basket inflation.
claims.next_test: Measure service-specific money and time cost per effective outcome beside household-type living-cost indexes.

claims.title: Participation measures choosing to work
claims.claim: Labour-force participation is the closest available proxy for whether needs being met causes people to choose not to work.
claims.rationale: Participation combines retirement, education, disability, caring, discouragement, policy, migration and voluntary choice.
counter_hypotheses: Participation declines because people cannot find suitable work or cannot combine work with care.
Working hours, job quality and desired hours change before participation.
falsifiers: Linked survey evidence shows participation changes are dominated by secure voluntary withdrawal in the relevant cohort.
claims.next_test: Use reasons for non-participation, desired hours, job-search status, security and longitudinal transitions.

claims.title: Eight instruments do not exist
claims.claim: Access margin, transition speed, concentration, preparedness, trust and cross-border access are unmeasured because the instruments do not exist.
claims.rationale: Partial official instruments exist. The honest statuses are not defined, not integrated, inaccessible, stale, not comparable or not validated.
counter_hypotheses: Existing datasets can answer useful narrower versions of each question.
The missing object is a join and validation protocol rather than an instrument.
falsifiers: A documented search finds no usable component measures for a precisely scoped service, cohort and jurisdiction.
claims.next_test: Create a source inventory and replace binary measurement status with a data-readiness state machine.
